title: Heidi Klum's Halloween costume revealed as Traitors' Maya Jama dresses as Mo Farah
description: From Maya as Sir Mo Farah to Heidi as her own left hand: The best Halloween looksFigure caption, Watch: Heidi Klum as a giant severed hand for 25th an
body: From Maya as Sir Mo Farah to Heidi as her own left hand: The best Halloween looksFigure caption, Watch: Heidi Klum as a giant severed hand for 25th annual Halloween bashByJacob PhillipsSupermodel and TV host Heidi Klum confirmed her position as the queen of Halloween by transforming into a giant, bloodied and severed hand for her annual costume party in New York.Klum, 53, was completely unrecognisable arriving at her event in what she described as her own chopped-off "left hand".This year marks the 25th anniversary of Klum's party, which brings celebrities across the globe together dressed in their wild, weird and wonderful costumes.And the revelry didn't stop there, with celebrities such as Maya Jama wowing attendees at her own Halloween party in London dressed as four-time Olympic champion Sir Mo Farah.Image source, Getty Images for Heidi KlumImage caption, Klum said her costume this year needed the help of up to 20 people to complete"It took a lot of hands putting this hand together," Klum told reporters as she posed for pictures on the red carpet. "I think about 10 or 20 hands."Explaining the inspiration for the idea, she said: "I looked at my hand and I thought 'Hey, I think that I can fit my body inside of this somehow.'"I always try to come up with something unusual and I don't think I've seen an actual person walking around like a hand. I thought that was something new and different."Klum is never one to shy away from dressing up on the scariest day of the year, with previous looks including a worm, Medusa and the ogre Princess Fiona from the Shrek films.Image source, Getty Images for Heidi Klum HalloweenImage caption, At the party, Klum later lost the full hand costumeOther attendees at Klum's party this year included actors Neil Patrick Harris and David Burtka, who surprised attendees by dressing as the twins from the horror film The Shining.Image source, Getty Images for Heidi KlumImage caption, Harris and his husband Burtka looked eerie in their matching outfitsPop star Jade Thirlwall also attended the party in New York dressed as a stone statue of an angel, while Severance and Spider-Man actor Tramell Tillman turned up with intricate face makeup and prosthetics.Image source, Getty Images for Heidi Klum HalloweenImage caption, Jade transformed herself to look like she was made of stoneImage source, Getty Images for Heidi Klum HalloweenImage caption, Tillman arrived with fake ears and tufts emerging from his foreheadMeanwhile in London, broadcaster Maya Jama hosted her annual Halloween Party dressed as Sir Mo Farah.Jama told Elle UK magazine she wanted to dress as the "bald headed icon" to honour the Olympian, adding that she has wanted to dress up as a man for years for Halloween."[Sir Mo] loved the idea," she explained."He's actually sent me all of his real life Olympic outfits, his real, actual medals he won for the Olympics."His real trainers. He's even done some TikToks for me. He is fully on board."Image source, Getty Images for Maya Jama Annual Halloween PartyImage caption, Jama celebrated Olympic champion Sir Mo FarahImage source, Getty Images for Maya Jama Annual Halloween PartyImage caption, Ryan recreated one of Jama's most talked-about Traitors looks

schema.headline: Heidi Klum's Halloween costume revealed as Traitors' Maya Jama dresses as Mo Farah

title: Five teenagers stabbed at Halloween party in Chandler's Ford
description: Five teenagers have been seriously injured after being stabbed at a Halloween party, police have said.Officers were called to Park Road in Chandler's
body: Five teenagers have been seriously injured after being stabbed at a Halloween party, police have said.Officers were called to Park Road in Chandler's Ford, near Eastleigh, shortly after 22:30 GMT on Saturday.The injured teens - three boys aged 16 and two aged 17 - were taken to hospital.Hampshire Police said it believes an unknown group gained entry to a party at an address on Park Road before the stabbings.The force has appealed for witnesses and anyone with information to come forward.A police cordon remained in place on Sunday while officers continue their investigation.Senior investigating officer Det Ch Insp Elizabeth Pirie acknowledged the impact on local residents and thanked the community for its patience.Earlier, an eyewitness told the BBC ambulances and an air ambulance had attended.Another eyewitness said they saw someone running out of the house involved, shouting that he had been stabbed and that he was being chased by two people.

schema.headline: Five teenagers stabbed at Halloween party in Chandler's Ford

title: Police probe video of officer hitting youth with handcuffs in Speke
description: In the video, the boy is punched in the stomach, chest and throat before he is handcuffed and dragged off the ground by the officer, then led to a pol
body: In the video, the boy is punched in the stomach, chest and throat before he is handcuffed and dragged off the ground by the officer, then led to a police van.Another teenager can be seen being pulled from the ground as he is arrested.After a complaint was made on Saturday, the force said its professional standards team would look into the incident."While we look to establish the full circumstances of what happened, we would urge people not to speculate and avoid sharing rumours or misinformation," the force said in a statement published on its website.The incident happened the night before Halloween, on what in Liverpool has become known as "Mischief Night"."We are determined to protect our communities from the sort of appalling behaviour that we historically see at this time of year. "We have a contempt for criminality and a commitment to cracking down on people committing serious offences in Merseyside," a force spokesman added.

schema.headline: Police probe video of officer hitting youth with handcuffs in Speke

title: Cate McHugh wins The Voice UK after being mentored by Sir Tom Jones
description: A singer who began her career as a teenager busking on the streets of Cardiff has been crowned winner of The Voice UK.Cate McHugh, from Llantwit Major
body: A singer who began her career as a teenager busking on the streets of Cardiff has been crowned winner of The Voice UK.Cate McHugh, from Llantwit Major in the Vale of Glamorgan, appeared stunned when she heard her name announced on the ITV show, telling viewers "I did it" when asked how she was feeling.The performer, who has a degenerative sight condition which has left her registered blind, was given a congratulatory hug by her coach Sir Tom Jones on his final appearance on the show after previously announcing he had been "fired". Speaking after the show, McHugh, 31, said: "I won The Voice! I'm entirely gobsmacked and absolutely haven't fully processed this information just yet."Footage shared by McHugh on social media showed her laughing and smiling with family and friends screaming in delight as they celebrated her victory at a watch party in Cardiff.McHugh's prizes include a £50,000 cash prize and a recording contract, with her first ever single, a cover of The Beatles classic Blackbird, now released.Posting on social media, she said: "From the bottom of my heart I want to say THANK YOU for following my journey, and joining my world! This is where it's going to REALLY get fun!"

schema.headline: Cate McHugh wins The Voice UK after being mentored by Sir Tom Jones

title: Stranded in the Cook Islands: Why I can't get home to Sri Lanka
description: I've been stuck on a tiny Pacific island for years and can't get a transit visa to fly homeImage source, SuppliedByAyeshea PereraAsia Digital Editor a
body: I've been stuck on a tiny Pacific island for years and can't get a transit visa to fly homeImage source, SuppliedByAyeshea PereraAsia Digital Editor and Dinuk HewawitharanaBBC SinhalaWhen Ruchira Ranasingha left Sri Lanka almost a decade ago, she could never have imagined she would end up stranded on a tiny archipelago in the South Pacific.The 50-year-old has now been stuck in the Cook Islands for three years. She tells the BBC she is desperate to go back to Sri Lanka and has even offered to go "handcuffed, bound and gagged".Ranasingha had been hoping to settle in New Zealand.After seeking asylum there, she says she followed an immigration adviser's recommendation to temporarily exit the country to apply for a work visa. But once in the Cook Islands, her application was rejected. And by leaving New Zealand, she had breached the terms of her existing asylum-linked visa.Now New Zealand is refusing to issue her a transit visa that would allow her to fly home to Sri Lanka.Australia is refusing too. The only other international destinations she can fly to from the Cook Islands - Tahiti and Hawaii - require her to give biometric information in New Zealand before any visa can be processed.As a result, she has no feasible way of leaving."My son - my only child - is getting married in November and I really want to be there for his wedding. My mother is so worried about what has happened to me that she is constantly in and out of hospital," she says through tears."I will do anything they ask of me - I just want to go home."Ranasingha left Sri Lanka in 2018 after being forced to close her small T-shirt factory due to a loss of business. Struggling to repay loans, she moved to Hong Kong to work as a domestic caregiver looking after elderly people and children.Her brother tells BBC Sinhala she had come under immense financial pressure. Her husband was a drug addict who died about seven years ago, he adds.In December 2022, Ranasingha headed to New Zealand, where she says she lived with a cousin on a two-month visit visa. As it came close to expiring, she says an immigration interpreter helped her apply for asylum on the grounds she was facing threats from lenders in Sri Lanka.She was granted an asylum seeker "open work visa", enabling her to work for almost any employer for a year. She found a job at a restaurant, she says, which ultimately agreed to sponsor an employment visa, which she believed would give her longer-term stability.But as asylum seekers generally cannot apply for other visas while their applications are processed in New Zealand, it was declined.That's when she got in touch with Immigration & Secretarial Services, a firm she claims told her a fresh application for an employment visa could be made from overseas. Email correspondence the BBC has seen shows its manager, Sylviane Gallant, saying she would initiate the process as soon as Ranasingha had left the country.So she booked a short stay in the Cook Islands while the application was made.It turned out to be a disastrous decision.Image source, AFP via Getty ImagesImage caption, Cook Islands is known for its beaches and volcanic peaks - but Ruchira Ranasingha is an involuntary guestShe was again refused the employment visa. And by leaving New Zealand, she had violated the terms of her existing visa. New Zealand authorities made it clear they would not grant her any future visas.Gallant claimed to make various interventions on her behalf, including writing to politicians including Chris Penk, New Zealand's then-immigration minister. But ultimately, Ranasingha says Gallant admitted the situation was her fault and told her "there was nothing more she could do"."She told me I was better off going home. There was nothing holding me there so I agreed to go."But when she turned up at the airport with an Air New Zealand ticket to Sri Lanka in hand, she was told she couldn't board the flight without a New Zealand transit visa.Three applications for a New Zealand transit visa were rejected. Authorities said they weren't convinced she would leave New Zealand. Four applications for Australian transit visas were rejected too.In one of its rejections, New Zealand suggested she explore other routes. But both the US state of Hawaii and the French Polynesian island of Tahiti told her she would need to provide biometric information before any visa could be processed - and that could only be done in person in New Zealand.Her latest application to New Zealand, which included all the details of the alternative routes she'd been trying, as well as her son's upcoming wedding and mother's failing health, was also rejected."I have lost so much money on tickets. For almost four years I have been just applying for visa after visa with nothing working out," she says, breaking down.Image source, SuppliedOn a collection of islands known for their sweeping sandy beaches and rugged volcanic peaks, just four hours from Auckland, Ranasingha has been an involuntary guest.She's luckier than others in her position, she says, with her hotel letting her stay free of charge in its staff accommodation and friendly locals providing her with food and clothing.One of the hotel directors even gave her a sewing machine, she says, enabling her to make a small income."My mother always tells me I must have done something good, for me to be in a place like this where people have been so kind to me," she tells the BBC.But it does little to ease the sense of being trapped.Ranasingha says the stress is impacting her health. "I am scared something is going to happen to me," she says."I don't know what her solution is, to be honest," says Auckland-based immigration law specialist Alastair McClymont.She had received "terrible advice" which "certainly" could not have come from a genuine immigration lawyer, he says, pointing to an industry of "so-called immigration consultants" who charge people to lodge applications without fully understanding the risks involved. Ranasingha says she has parted with thousands of New Zealand dollars in fees to Immigration & Secretarial Services.The BBC reached out to Gallant but did not receive a response.McClymont suggests New Zealand authorities will not grant the transit visa because, as far as they are concerned, she has no intention of returning to Sri Lanka having made an asylum claim saying her life was in danger there.New Zealand co-ordinates with its neighbour Australia which means it won't want to let her transit either, he says, and France and the US are likely to reach similar conclusions.To leave, "she is going to have to transit through somewhere and no-one will want to take the risk."Immigration New Zealand told the BBC it had received multiple transit visa applications from Ranasingha - all declined "as we were not satisfied she has a genuine intention to transit through New Zealand".When asked why one couldn't be granted even when Ranasingha had offered to be handcuffed and escorted, a representative of the immigration minister's office said those measures do not prevent individuals from making an asylum claim.Australia's Home Affairs department said it would not comment on individual cases. It said any non-citizens travelling to Australia "must satisfy the requirements of the Migration Act 1958 (the Act) and the Migration Regulations 1994".Meanwhile, Ranasingha's family have been trying to see if the Sri Lankan government can help. Her brother says they have tried "every possible avenue... but so far we haven't been able to get anywhere on this".Sri Lanka's foreign ministry told the BBC it was "taking all necessary steps to facilitate her return to Sri Lanka from the Cook Islands. Officials of the Sri Lankan High Commission in Wellington, New Zealand, as well as the relevant New Zealand authorities, are working closely with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs on this matter."But Ranasingha's brother is deeply worried."Her mental state is not good," he tells BBC Sinhala."One of the times we spoke, she told me that if they were not willing to get her back home alive, they might at least repatriate her body."Additional reporting by Kethaki Masilamani and Julianna KhanIf you've been affected by issues involving suicide or feelings of despair, details of organisations offering advice and support for people in the UK are available from BBC Action Line. Help and support outside the UK can be found at Befrienders Worldwide, external.

schema.headline: Stranded in the Cook Islands: Why I can't get home to Sri Lanka

title: John Healey risks breaking minimum wage promise for younger workers
description: The Chancellor, John Healey, has suggested that younger workers might not receive the same minimum wage as others before the next election, potentiall
body: The Chancellor, John Healey, has suggested that younger workers might not receive the same minimum wage as others before the next election, potentially breaking a Labour manifesto promise. In 2024, Labour said it would remove "discriminatory age bands", vowing to end the gap between the adult minimum wage and pay for 18 to 20-year-olds.But in last week's Budget, Healey said that younger workers would see the same increase as older workers, leaving a gap between the two rates this year.  Pay for 18 to 20-year-olds in 2026 will rise to £11.27, while over-20s will be paid a minimum of £13.21 an hour. In a BBC interview broadcast on Sunday, Healey was asked if younger workers would be paid the same as older workers, when it comes to the minimum wage, by the time of the next election?"We'll take one step at a time," he said, suggesting that Labour might abandon its plan to close the gap before the next election. It is a change that is likely to anger the unions and some on the left of the party.Healey added that Labour was still committed to the ambition, but hinted the plan to equalise wages might be delayed, partly to encourage businesses to employ younger workers. "There is no question about whether or if, it's a question of when - it's a question of how fast," he said. "I want to make sure we can look hard at those trade-offs that are there between jobs and wages.""I want to take business, I want to take trade unions with me, and with the government, because together we have to get into what at the moment is a moral shame on this nation. A million youngsters - written off without any prospect of being helped into work and making contributions to this country for the future."The chancellor also suggested that he is willing to make potentially big cuts to some areas of public spending, to get the country's debt falling. The budget documents spell out real-terms reductions to some government departments in the years to come. The likelihood of the government following through was questioned by the respected independent number cruncher, the Institute for Fiscal Studies (IFS) this week. But asked if he would make big cuts, Healey said: "We've already demonstrated we are prepared to take hard decisions about the priorities in government."Pressed on whether he would make cuts of more than 2% a year to some government departments, he added: "We will carry that through to the 10-year plan and the spending review next year.""But in the budget I also set out the ways that we're preparing and the work we've got under way to prepare for those spending review decisions."Conservative Party leader Kemi Badenoch said the "bulk" of spending cuts should be from the welfare budget, describing it as containing "astronomical sums".She also proposed reducing the size of the civil service and reducing budgets in departments such as the Department for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport.On whether she would support cuts pencilled in by the government, Badenoch told the same programme: "What exactly are they cutting? I'm not against what they're doing but there's no detail."Badenoch said she did not want to see cuts in frontline services but said there was a need to "bring down the cost of government".Reflecting on the Budget, she said: "The chancellor had 98 different measures, a lot of them very piecemeal, none will make a difference."So living within our means, absolutely, we've got to do that. That will require cuts to government, but we are setting out the things very clearly that we're going to change, the bulk of which is in welfare. Other departments will have changes too."

schema.headline: John Healey risks breaking minimum wage promise for younger workers

title: Ciara Mageean: Tributes to 'inspirational' Olympic athlete after death at 34
description: Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption, A statement posted on Mageean's social media on Sunday said she died surrounded by her loved onesByBen Lonsda
body: Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption, A statement posted on Mageean's social media on Sunday said she died surrounded by her loved onesByBen LonsdaleBBC News NIUpdated 29 minutes agoTributes have been paid to former European champion and two-time Olympic runner Ciara Mageean, who has died at the age of 34.Mageean, from Portaferry in County Down, was diagnosed with stage four bowel cancer in May 2025.She died on Sunday morning, surrounded by her loved ones, a statement posted on her social media accounts said."A beloved daughter, sister, wife, friend and inspiration to so many, she will be deeply missed," it said.Mageean's death comes less than three weeks after her marriage to her long-term partner Thomas Moran.The athlete represented Ireland at the 2016 and 2020 Olympics and won gold in the 1500m at the European Athletics Championships in Rome in 2024.She also represented Northern Ireland at the Commonwealth Games, winning silver in Birmingham in 2022.'One of our own'Olympic legend Lady Mary Peters said Mageean was a "wonderful lady" who was "gracious, beautiful, talented and inspirational to the next generation"."We knew she was very ill and we knew that it was inevitable but we didn't expect it so soon," said the 1972 Olympic pentathlon gold medallist.Lady Mary's charity the Mary Peters Trust, which supports Northern Ireland athletes, had helped Mageean in her athletics career."My charity supported her for as long as we could because she was so talented and we recognised that in her," said Lady Mary.She said that Mageean had continued to inspire young athletes even while undergoing treatment for cancer and would be "sorely missed in the world of sport".Image source, EPAImage caption, Mageean won a gold medal at the 2024 European Championships in RomeSean Young, the secretary of Portaferry Gaelic Athletic Club, where Mageean played camogie in her younger years, said its members were in "disbelief and shock" at her death.He said Mageean had been a "fierce competitor" who began her sporting journey at the club before pursuing athletics."Outside the sporting arena she is the most inspirational, humble person we have ever had within our club," he said.Down Gaelic Athletic Association (GAA) said it was "honoured and privileged" to call Mageean one of its own, describing her as someone who never forgot her roots."She touched the lives of so many people and she helped change the lives of so many," it said."In her battle with illness she showed us courage, positivity and the value of life."Her former school, Assumption Grammar in Ballynahinch, County Down, said it was "deeply saddened and heartbroken" by the death of its "cherished past pupil"."Ciara's kindness, strength, faith and unwavering determination were an inspiration to us all," it said."She touched countless lives with her warmth, humility and generosity of spirit."'A champion in every sense of the word'Northern Ireland's First Minister Michelle O'Neill described Mageean as "a champion in every sense of the word and a role model for all athletes"."She represented her country with pride and helped put Irish athletics on the map," said O'Neill.She said Mageean had faced her cancer diagnosis with the same "bravery and determination" she had shown throughout her sporting career."Ciara's legacy will live on and she will continue to be an inspiration to many."Deputy First Minister Emma Little-Pengelly said people across Northern Ireland had been "deeply proud and inspired" by the athlete.She described Mageean as an "outstanding athlete and ambassador for her sport" who had spoken with honesty and bravery about her health battles.Figure caption, Mageean clinched her first major title at the age of 32 Irish President Catherine Connolly said Mageean had stood out for "her strength and perseverance, for her clear speaking and for her determination to succeed"."It was these qualities that led the public to appreciate her so much and to be so thrilled for her achievement in Rome," said Connolly."Since Ciara shared the news of her illness, the public have stood with her and their affection for her has only grown."Taoiseach (Irish Prime Minister) Micheál Martin said he was "deeply saddened" by her untimely death and extended his sympathies to her husband, family and friends.Tánaiste (Irish Deputy Prime Minister) Simon Harris said Mageean had inspired people both through her achievements on the track and her openness about her illness."She gave so many others strength and hope," he said.'Self-belief and commitment'World Athletics described her as "an inspiration to many, on and off the track", highlighting her historic European gold medal in Rome in 2024.Athletics Ireland, the country's governing body for the sport, said Mageean was "much-loved and inspirational"."Her courage, warmth and spirit will leave a lasting legacy," the organisation said.Conal Heatley, the chief executive of Commonwealth Games Northern Ireland, described Mageean as "one of the best of us".He told BBC News NI she had carried herself with "incredible dignity" throughout her illness and was a "fantastic figure for the island of Ireland".The Camogie Association also paid tribute to Mageean, with its president Brian Molloy describing her as a great friend of the sport, both as a player and a supporter."In her all-too-short life, Ciara touched the hearts of so many," he said."Her self-belief and commitment to her craft will always be inspirational and she will be fondly remembered by all who had the privilege of knowing her."'A light has gone out in the world'Mageean was named the 2023 BBC Northern Ireland Sports Personality of the Year after an impressive year, in which she broke national records and was fourth in a competitive World Championships final.BBC Sport NI broadcaster Thomas Niblock, who interviewed Mageean in July for The GAA Social podcast, described her as a "one off".Image source, Thomas NiblockImage caption, Thomas Niblock (left) recalled how Mageean had received disappointing news the day before their interview"A light has gone out in the world. Authentic, talented, decent. Her kindness and wonderful personality was a joy to watch and see," he wrote on social media.Niblock recalled how Mageean had received disappointing news the day before their interview but had insisted on going ahead with the recording."It's 90 minutes [co-presenter] Oisin [McConville] and myself will always treasure. She was the best of us," he said.He also paid tribute to her husband and the wider Portaferry community."I've never met a person who met Ciara, who didn't love her," he added.Patrick Kielty, who said it was a "privilege" to interview Mageean on Irish national broadcaster RTÉ's The Late Late Show, said "she wasn't just a champion on the track"."She was a champion of others who showed us all how to live."

schema.headline: Ciara Mageean: Tributes to 'inspirational' Olympic athlete after death at 34

title: Liverpool 0-1 Arsenal: Gunners make history at Anfield as they continue title defence
description: "Today has to be the day."That is what manager Mikel Arteta said before Arsenal secured their first Premier League win at Anfield in 14 years, beating
body: "Today has to be the day."That is what manager Mikel Arteta said before Arsenal secured their first Premier League win at Anfield in 14 years, beating Liverpool thanks to Kai Havertz's first-half goal.Arteta was Arsenal captain the last time the Gunners won at Liverpool - 2-0 in 2012 - and they have had 16 unsuccessful trips in all competitions until Sunday's victory. The Spaniard's side, as they so often do, produced a defensive masterclass to keep out wave after wave of Liverpool attack to deliver a rare and historic win.Arsenal travelled to Anfield after an embarrassing loss to League Two Fleetwood Town in the Carabao Cup on Tuesday. Arteta said he thought that humbling loss in Lancashire could spur his side on to a historic win at Liverpool."Extremely proud. It's been 14 years, that's a long time," Arteta said after the game."I'm sure we made everybody attached to the club extremely proud today. Not only for the victory but for the way we've done it, the spirit we've shown. "Especially considering what happened four days ago when you lose and go out of the cup against a team you are supposed to beat. That's the magical part of this game, it can take you to really bad places but four days later you have the opportunity to do something really historic and we've done it."Overall, to win against a team that is producing what they are doing, and also in the emotional state after Fleetwood, that's what a winning team should do."Before the match, centre-back Gabriel said that Arsenal were expecting a "big battle" and "big chaos" against Liverpool.That prediction was correct and, after going ahead, Arsenal were pinned back before the break.Although the second half was a bit calmer, they still defended resolutely and did not allow Liverpool a shot on target. The Gunners, who have kept six clean sheets this season, are now three points clear at the top of the table after nine games. Arsenal's 24 points is the most by any team after nine games of a season since the Gunners themselves in 2022-23. And only in the 2004-05 and 2007-08 seasons have Arsenal had more at this stage of a Premier League season. "It means a lot to our football club," match winner Havertz said after the win. "It's been 13 games [in the Premier League without a win here], its a crazy stat and it's what the fans deserve. We are happy we gave them that."The win was also the first time that Arsenal had kept a clean sheet at Anfield in the Premier League since that victory in 2012. "That is the Anfield way, that is what this Liverpool team can do, this is what this stadium does to you," Declan Rice - who assisted Havertz's goal - added. "It just creates waves and waves of attack."We've not won here in 14 years. It was relentless attacks but in the end that way we stuck together, that togetherness we have is undefeated. It's nothing like I've ever seen before."Rice has been one of Arsenal's standout players this season and has five assists in the league already Arsenal are now two points better off after nine games of this campaign than last season, when they won the title. The Gunners attack is not yet flowing and they have scored just 14 league goals in nine gamesArteta has been restricted with his options in the forward line with Bukayo Saka out injured, 16-year-old Max Dowman suspended after his red card at Fleetwood, Christos Tzolis just back from a hamstring injury, and Viktor Gyokeres and Havertz both struggling for form. But the Arsenal defence is an elite unit. The back four only conceded 27 goals last season and, on this performance, they could once again be the difference for the Gunners. "I'm extremely proud; this is something you want to accomplish." Arteta said after being asked what the win against Liverpool means to him. "That's the challenge and mission you want to accomplish. I love it when it's something we have not done for many years. "It was the same with Chelsea away and Manchester United away. To be able to beat all those, that's the purpose and motivation and why we do what we do."Manchester City are second in the table but are waiting to find out what happens, pending their appeal, following their charge for breaching the Premier League financial rules. And with the rest of the big-name sides in the league in a period of transition, Arsenal could find themselves with a healthy lead at the top of the table of the table if things carry on as they are.

schema.headline: Liverpool 0-1 Arsenal: Gunners make history at Anfield as they continue title defence

title: Celebrity Traitors: Why the real winners are Maya Jama, King Kenny and Miranda Hart
description: Image source, BBC/Studio LambertByNoor NanjiCulture correspondentSpoiler warning: This article reveals details from The Celebrity Traitors finalIn som
body: Image source, BBC/Studio LambertByNoor NanjiCulture correspondentSpoiler warning: This article reveals details from The Celebrity Traitors finalIn some ways, all the players on The Celebrity Traitors can be seen as winners.They all got to appear on a hugely popular TV show, rubbing shoulders with other stars and gaining new fans along the way.But there are certain celebrities, such as Miranda Hart, King Kenny, Maya Jama and Joanne McNally, who have been tipped by industry experts as getting the biggest career boost after the show.Sebastian "Bash" Croft - who won the game, alongside Romesh Ranganathan - could also now be in line for greater roles.We've taken a look at the breakout stars of the series and what might lie ahead for them.Miranda HartAfter a spell of ill-health, the show has done wonders for bringing Miranda Hart back into the public eye.There was that incredible “Little Mix Big Mix” viral dance moment, but Hart also displayed a level of vulnerability which stood out in a show where the stars don't really talk about their personal lives.When her friend Joe Lycett was banished, her tearful reaction to his exit provided a rare poignant moment."Connection and laughter and joy are bigger than this game - and to meet someone and just play and laugh, it's all us humans need, you know?" she said.When she was murdered, she also demonstrated genuine emotion in her response. "Ultimately, in my little personal story, this has been quite extraordinary," she said.For culture journalist Natalie Jamieson, Hart's openness and relatability made her the "standout" star from this year's series.And it could also lead to us seeing more of Hart on the small screen. According to The Sun, external, the BBC is looking to bring back her self-titled sitcom after her stint on Celebrity Traitors led to fresh interest in the show.Image source, BBC/Studio LambertThe BBC declined to comment on the possible return of Hart’s show.But she’s not the only one who won hearts by showing real warmth.The same could be said for Romesh Ranganathan - who, in a departure from his usual cynical, deadpan stand-up persona, seemed really to care about his fellow cast members. Jerry Hall also won viewers over with her charming eccentricity.And then there’s James Acaster, who showed genuine vulnerability as he struggled to come to terms with being a traitor.Social media users seemed split after his bombshell confession to being a traitor, with some totally exasperated and others saying they respected him for going out on his own terms. Either way, he's definitely got the nation talking.King KennyWhen it comes to celebrities who are most likely to see the biggest career boost, most experts say Kenny is King.Going into the castle, the 29-year-old was best known to younger fans as a member of the popular British YouTube collective Beta Squad.But Kenny will have been "the least familiar name to a mainstream audience," says showbiz journalist Nikki Onafuye.That all changed as he was recruited as a traitor, bringing much-needed energy to the turret - and he made it all the way through to Friday night’s tense final.Having shown he can hold his own alongside established broadcasters, actors and comedians, big things could now be in store for Kenny."He 100% has just been minted as a mainstream star now," said Marina Hyde, on The Rest is Entertainment podcast.“The next steps could be panel shows, presenting roles, reality competitions or entertainment formats,” adds TV reporter Siobhan Synnot.Maya JamaFellow traitor Maya Jama also sailed all the way to the final with her cool-as-a-cucumber persona making her a traitor to be reckoned with.Despite being banished in dramatic fashion, she could now be in line to receive £1m per deal, according to a report in The Times earlier this week, external.What Celebrity Traitors has done for Jama is allow her to reveal more of her personality than on Love Island, says Onafuye.But TV reporter Synnot thinks between the two, Kenny has more to gain because he has introduced himself to millions of new viewers - whereas Jama was already one of Britain's best-known TV presenters before Celebrity Traitors."Maya's gain is subtler: she can emerge looking less like the presenter of Love Island and more like a genuinely versatile television star," she says.Joanne McNallyOf all the comedians in the castle, Joanne McNally was initially the least well known, says Caroline Frost, TV editor at Radio Times.But she flourished on the show, lasting right up to Thursday's semi-final."And she's taken her own path, ignoring the herd and making her own voting decisions, sometimes chaotically, but always with charm, wit and good humour,” says Frost.The Irish comedian's podcast was already popular before the show.But after her stint as the joker of the pack, bigger things could now lie in store for her.Just a few days ago, it was announced, external that her stand-up tour has been extended into 2027, "due to phenomenal demand".And her agents will be "fielding calls" for her to bring her star power to other shows, adds Frost.As it happened: Relive the Celebrity Traitors finalCulture journalist Jamieson says some of the other female contestants - such as Sharon Rooney, Leigh-Anne Pinnock and Myha'la - also stood out for showing their wit and wisdom, which could serve them well in the outside world.Things got a bit awkward in one of the episodes, when Sharon disagreed with some of the cast on a challenge, with some social media users saying she was acting in a "childish" way.But others argued it was a classic case of women being drowned out by men."There's been a subtlety in the smartness of women on display here, alongside the frustration of not always being listened to in the game," says Jamieson.Sebastian 'Bash' CroftIn the end, it was faithful duo Romesh Ranganathan and Sebastian ‘Bash’ Croft who emerged victorious.Comedian Ranganathan was already a huge star, but the show has introduced Croft, 24, to a much wider audience.He’s had previous acting roles in Game of Thrones and Heartstopper, but Traitors allowed him to show his own personality, "which as we've seen has endeared him both to other players and the huge watching audience", says Frost.He is also building his career as a pop star, and he's had a strong presence on social media during the series, posting videos of his tracks.His debut EP comes out later in November, perfect timing to capitalise on his Traitors win.And what's in store for the others...What's clear is that the true victors aren't necessarily the ones who get their hands on the prize pot.Arguably, what matters most is the amount of screen time you get - and what you do with it.On that note, spare a thought for those who left the show early, such as Amol Rajan, Julie Hesmondhalgh and Hannah Fry.But all made an impact in their own way and, as Synnot points out, they get "a nice anecdote" for future interviews.And what of James Blunt, who stole hearts with his military approach to the challenges and eccentric Top Gun-style outfits - and who came so close to winning the whole show?Maybe he's the mystery man in contention for the new James B(ond) - although his hapless theories could mean he'll be in line to be the new Johnny English instead.

schema.headline: Celebrity Traitors: Why the real winners are Maya Jama, King Kenny and Miranda Hart

title: Hull adventurer Karl Bushby 'overwhelmed' at Humber Bridge crowds
description: The adventurer has said the opportunity to embark on his walk came after the breakdown of his marriage, when his wife returned to Northern Ireland wit
body: The adventurer has said the opportunity to embark on his walk came after the breakdown of his marriage, when his wife returned to Northern Ireland with their son."When I left home and I walked down south first of all to test the machine that I first had, I don't remember any of that journey except for the Humber Bridge," he said on Sunday."There's that mystic look to it where you can't see the other side of the river."It's kind of almost symbolic."The Humber Bridge has always been that iconic landmark in my mind."Aged 29, Bushby said he walked out of Punta Arenas, Chile, with a few hundred dollars in his pocket and turned north for home.By the time he swum back across the English Channel on 5 October, Bushby, now 57, had crossed four continents, a frozen sea, deserts, mountains and jungles.

schema.headline: Hull adventurer Karl Bushby 'overwhelmed' at Humber Bridge crowds

title: Henry Nowak: Southampton student’s family on police footage
description: Officers went to Lucy's home at the same time. "We got that dreaded knock on the door at one o'clock in the morning," she said."They said to me, 'Do y
body: Officers went to Lucy's home at the same time. "We got that dreaded knock on the door at one o'clock in the morning," she said."They said to me, 'Do you have a son called Henry?… There's been an altercation. And unfortunately, your son has passed away'."No words, no words can explain that feeling."Olivia said she rang her father after hearing the news. "I just remember this scream. It was awful. He screamed 'My boy, my boy'," she said.She now keeps some of Henry's T-shirts on his bed and told ITV they still smell of him and give her comfort.But Lucy said she could no longer enter his bedroom because of the memories it holds."I can't go in there," she said.Coats now hang over the bedroom door so she does not have to look at it as she passes.

schema.headline: Henry Nowak: Southampton student’s family on police footage

title: Kimi Antonelli - the boy 'born in a garage' and made on the track
description: This is an updated version of an article first published in August 2026Kimi Antonelli was 10 when his father Marco first realised the boy sitting on h
body: This is an updated version of an article first published in August 2026Kimi Antonelli was 10 when his father Marco first realised the boy sitting on his lap, operating the steering and gears, might have an exceptional talent as a racing driver.The pair were at the Adria circuit in north-east Italy, Marco with his Lamborghini sports car team, Kimi competing in a karting race.It was the end of the day and Marco, a former driver himself, asked his son: "Do you want to try the Lamborghini?"Of course he did.Marco strapped himself and Kimi into the car, belts extended around both. Dad was in charge of the throttle and brake, his son would control the rest."I couldn't see the track because he was in front of me with a helmet on," Marco tells BBC Sport. "I could only see beside me the marker panels before each corner - 100m, 50m."We started to drive, step by step, faster, faster, faster. In the end, I pushed like I was alone and I arrived at the braking point at the end of the straight, 320km/h, braked very hard and at the limit."The car had a lot of oversteer. Kimi controlled the oversteer perfectly, then I went on the throttle, Kimi finished the oversteer, changed gear, and went."I said: 'OK, stop, because it has now become dangerous.' But when I saw the video, 10 years old, on my leg, oversteer, everything perfect, I said: 'Maybe he has something special.'"And now Kimi, who turned 20 only in August, has dominated F1 in only his second season, and become the youngest world champion in the sport's history.This is the story of a boy his dad says was "born in a garage".Marco Antonelli did not originally want his son to become a racing driver, because of his own struggles during his career."Sometimes you are fast but not in the right position to become a professional driver," he says.In the 1990s, Marco Antonelli was on the cusp of becoming a works driver in the DTM touring car series, then a huge hit with audiences across Europe.He tested for Alfa Romeo, but then the team boss left and the opportunity evaporated. Another chance came up with BMW, alongside Roberto Ravaglia and Steve Soper - stars at the time. Again, the same thing happened."I suffered a lot for it," Marco says. "And, of course, I was scared that my son [would] relive the same situation. At the beginning, I was very stressed about the passion my son had for motorsport."Kimi tried a go-kart for the first time when he was five, and immediately showed an awareness of racing lines, braking points and car control.The Antonellis were what Marco describes as "a normal family". They could not possibly afford to pay for Kimi to take part in all the categories on the way to Formula 1.Marco decided he could fund Kimi through karting and a year of the basic single-seater category, Formula 4. After that, he figured he might be able to put him in one of his GT cars and become professional that way.But Kimi immediately started to impress. Whatever category he entered, he was quick, and won.By now, Mercedes team boss Toto Wolff was already thinking that Antonelli would be his next F1 driver, potentially a replacement for Lewis Hamilton. With the seven-time champion approaching 40, Wolff was planning on taking control of that generational transition.So when it came time to negotiate a new contract with Hamilton in 2023, Wolff played hardball. Hamilton wanted to sign for at least two firm years, Wolff only one. In the end, they compromised on a contract for 2024 with an option for 2025.Hamilton, unimpressed, decided to look at his options, and signed to join Ferrari in 2025, telling Wolff in late January 2024, before the start of that season.Wolff immediately phoned Marco Antonelli, to tell him the "very big news"."'We put Kimi in Formula 1,'" Marco remembers Wolff saying. "'What do you think?'"I said: 'Oh, [it] is a difficult question you ask me. Of course I'm happy that you think about Kimi but are you sure he's ready?'"Mercedes were at a management away day. Wolff called his senior engineers together to tell them about Hamilton's decision."We were reviewing options and trying to come to a fairly rapid conclusion," says trackside engineering director Andrew Shovlin."We were all keen to just go with Kimi, which we knew was a bit of a risk. But it was quite exciting and we thought, based on his career to date, he had a good chance of being very good. It seemed like a good challenge."Antonelli had not even driven an F1 car when Wolff made the call. Mercedes put together a testing programme for him, 20-odd days in cars a couple of years old at tracks all over the world to prepare him for his F1 debut in 2025.Shovlin and the engineers were immediately impressed."It was how rapidly he would get up to speed," Shovlin says. "What you normally see with drivers is they're just incrementally going a little bit quicker, braking a bit later."If you compare with other drivers we've seen in an F1 car for the first time, the best I'd ever seen until then was George [Russell]. You suddenly saw someone who was quite similar."With Kimi, he took a couple of runs to work out how the car behaved and then he'd be more or less on the limit."The other thing you can see is the fidelity of the car control, how they can sit with it right on the edge of breaking away from them on entry to a corner, but they can just control it in that condition."Equally, when you looked at the mistakes he was making, they were often errors of judgement or lack of experience. They weren't run-out-of-talent mistakes."Antonelli made one of these at the 2024 Italian Grand Prix. Wolff decided to give him his first experience of an F1 weekend in first practice at his home race at Monza.It was a spectacular debut - for both good and bad reasons.Antonelli set the fastest time on his first lap. Then he went for another. He was flying, miles quicker than anyone up to that point, but then he crashed heavily at the final corner, Parabolica."No-one on earth could have got the car around the corner at the speed he was attempting," Shovlin says. "He clearly got into his head that he would try and do something special and it was an error of judgment."Wolff took Antonelli aside, told him it was OK, and not to worry about it. But the crash had a significant impact on Antonelli.Wolff was very clear in public about managing expectations of Antonelli going into his debut season."I conditioned myself so strong that I said: 'There's going to be moments of brilliance and moments where you want to tear your hair out'," Wolff says.There were stand-out moments, including pole for the sprint in Miami.But the middle part of the season, through Europe, was a disappointment. A change to the rear suspension design made the car nervous and rocked his confidence. His pace was not impressive, and he made too many mistakes."We expected more highlights from him," Shovlin says.Marco Antonelli explains: "Mercedes needed to have a good result after a period that was not like the Hamilton era. And, of course, needed two cars that always take points."Kimi felt this necessity. The crash in Monza was very tough for him to forget. It created on him a big pressure."Wolff said the "moments of brilliance were there" but then there was "a spell of nine races that was really not good"."Me, personally, I never doubted," says Wolff. "Other people doubted. In the team and externally."A year on from his practice debut, Antonelli crashed again in Monza practice."This was the point where I said: 'Kimi, you've got to turn this around. This is just not good enough'," says Wolff. "He said: 'I know.'"Marco Antonelli says he and his son talked a lot during this period and that Kimi "understood that everything can change"."The period was bad but you can see light at the end of the tunnel," he says. "And step by step he started to take confidence."Once F1 had left Europe in the autumn of last year, there was a shift."Suddenly, we felt like we were making really good progress," says Shovlin."There were signs towards the end of the year. I'm not saying any of us thought we'd see what we've seen so far this year, but that we had a decent F1 driver."Antonelli has been rather more than that this year. He took the season by storm, and established a consistent supremacy over Russell.In the best car in the field, Antonelli took six poles and six wins in the first 11 races, establishing a 50-point lead in the championship.Mercedes lost their dominant form in the second half of the season in the face of challenges from first McLaren and then Red Bull.But Antonelli remained a consistent threat at the front, and he killed off his Monza ghosts in the Italian Grand Prix with a stunning victory after an engine penalty led to him starting 19th on the grid.He put in a drive of clinical excellence and, with help from a safety car, chased down and caught Russell in the final laps to take a win that will go down in folklore.The extent of his turnaround in form has shocked almost everyone."We were all surprised," Wolff says. "My thoughts were always that he needed to make the experience of knowing all the tracks, the pressure of performing on such a high level under the spotlight of the media, the constant public feedback, whether you're doing well or not, the situations everyone wanted to be close to him."There wasn't one single defining factor where I would have said that made it difficult for him, but this year, he knew exactly what to expect. What was really nice to see is that the self-confidence, without feeling any entitlement, has shone."Marco points to his son's "very strong" mentality."In F4 and Freca, he started with not good results, and he was able to remake everything and, at the end, work hard and win the championship," he says."We talk about F1. I don't know what the spark is in his brain, but Kimi in the past did the same."Verstappen says: "For me, there was never any doubt that he would make the jump the year after and already be a lot more consistently competitive."It's normal in the progression of a driver. In your rookie season, it can be quite tough, but at the moment, of course, he's doing an amazing job."Kimi pays tribute to his father, describing him as his "rock", while Wolff also praises the driver's "typical Italian family"."They are caring, they are loving," Wolff says. "Kimi's character, he's gentle, he has empathy, he has charisma, he has the right amount of intelligence for being a racing driver."Mercedes have been talking to Antonelli about managing his emotions, which have flared at times this season, such as in the sprint in Canada, when the racing between the two Mercedes drivers came close to boiling over.Shovlin says: "He just says: 'I'm young, I'm Italian, what do you expect?'"The remark reveals Antonelli's sense of humour, but also a maturity and self-awareness that might not always be expected in someone so young.Wolff says: "He has all that. He's actually not [fitting the stereotype of] a typical emotional Italian. He's so clear [in] what he needs to do in a car. I don't see lots of emotion. I see full focus, full concentration. I see, 'OK, this is a problem, let's analyse it, and move on.'"You see him in a debrief afterwards. You couldn't really say whether there was a bad or a good session. It's all very balanced and stable."Antonelli took advice on this when he met tennis legend Roger Federer at Wimbledon this summer."We chatted about my races," Antonelli says. "About when he used to play, and about life in general."About pressure, he just told me to focus on one race at a time, just focus on what you can control, and also to control the emotions, especially the ones that can make you do mistakes."Federer's words echoed something Marco has always impressed on his son."In our family, we use this concept in normal life as well," he says. "We have to live every day our best day. You work hard every day to arrive at the end of the project you have."Back in February 2024, Wolff followed up his phone call to Marco with a meeting in Milan."Toto said 'Of course it will be difficult, but I think after one year of experience, we can do very well with Kimi in F1'," Marco says."The project was 2025 experience, 2026 start to achieve results. I think we overachieved."

schema.headline: Kimi Antonelli - the boy 'born in a garage' and made on the track

title: Democrat Haley Stevens endorses Republican in Michigan Senate race
description: A Democrat in Michigan has endorsed the Republican candidate in the state's crucial US Senate contest, as a spat with her own party's candidate Abdul
body: A Democrat in Michigan has endorsed the Republican candidate in the state's crucial US Senate contest, as a spat with her own party's candidate Abdul El-Sayed escalated just days before the vote.Haley Stevens, a sitting congresswoman who lost out on the Democratic Senate nomination to El-Sayed, made a surprise appearance alongside the Republican candidate Mike Rogers on Sunday."I don't belong in Abdul's campaign," she said in a video posted to X shortly after that appearance. "Who we are as Michiganders is not hate and is not what we are getting out from our Democratic nominee right now.""That's why I am endorsing Mike Rogers," Stevens said.The move stunned many of Stevens' fellow Democrats who condemned her decision to break from the party and switch her support just two days before the election. The public feud between Stevens, a centrist Democrat, and El-Sayed, who represents the party's left-wing, has boiled over in recent days. Stevens called on El-Sayed to denounce a campaign advert from an outside liberal group that linked US support for Israel with high prices. El-Sayed criticised the advert and said he had nothing to do with its contents.Stevens had been scheduled to appear at an event with El-Sayed on Sunday in an effort to display party unity, but he reportedly asked her not to come and she chose to attend a church service with his Republican opponent instead."This is a very close election, we all know that, but Abdul made clear that I was not welcome in his campaign, that he didn't need me there, that he didn't want me there," Stevens told reporters as she stood alongside Rogers outside the church.When asked about Stevens' endorsement, El-Sayed told reporters he was focused on the problems Michiganders are facing."At the end of the day, I don't think about Haley Stevens," he said on Sunday. "None of this matters."In downtown Detroit, several Democrats the BBC spoke to said they were disappointed by Stevens' endorsement of Rogers."I just genuinely don't understand it," she said. "I do think it's a betrayal of the party because the things she stands for are not the same things that he stands for as a Republican.""Maybe she had frustrations with the party," Matthew Barera, another Michigan voter, said.Others, including Republicans who support Rogers, said they doubted it would make a difference to the race."People can see right through her actions, you know? She's just angry," Marissa Lee, a Rogers supporter, told the BBC. "She is not going to make anybody change their mind."Over the weekend, as Stevens' criticism of El-Sayed escalated, a number of Democratic politicians in Michigan publicly encouraged her to end the feud and back the party's candidates more directly.On Sunday, Democratic Senator Chuck Schumer called Stevens' endorsement of Rogers "a despicable betrayal" of her political party. After a bruising and sometimes bitter campaign earlier this year, El-Sayed, a left-wing outsider, defeated Stevens, the establishment-backed congresswoman, to win the party's nomination for the US Senate race.The primary, and the pair's subsequent feud, has underlined divisions over the party's direction ahead of the 2028 presidential election.Former public health official El-Sayed, who is the son of Egyptian immigrants, has channelled grassroots frustration with Washington politics as well as US ties to Israel.Stevens is a more centrist Democrat - and had the support of party figures such as Michigan Governor Gretchen Whitmer during the primary race. The party is hoping to regain control of the Senate in Tuesday's elections, but will need a net gain of four seats to do so. A loss in Michigan - which they currently hold - would represent a major blow and leave them needing to flip five seats.

schema.headline: Democrat Haley Stevens endorses Republican in Michigan Senate race

title: Russian strikes cut power to thousands in Ukraine as Kherson ceasefire ends
description: A rare humanitarian ceasefire in Ukraine's front-line Kherson region that allowed civilians to evacuate the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky has ended
body: A rare humanitarian ceasefire in Ukraine's front-line Kherson region that allowed civilians to evacuate the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky has ended.The localised ceasefire was due to end at 22:59 Ukrainian time (21:00 GMT) on Sunday. While the truce had held since it was implemented last week, fighting had continued elsewhere.On Sunday evening, Ukraine's air alert system was apparently hacked, the country's air force said, warning of radiation over Kyiv - a reference to a possible nuclear attack. The Air Force message read: "The Air Alarm application has probably been subjected to hostile interference. There is no radiation threat! Stay calm and follow our updates on our channel."Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said Russia had struck energy infrastructure in four regions overnight on Saturday, leaving hundreds of thousands of homes without power. Some connections were restored on Sunday.Another overnight strike killed two people, including a 13-year-old girl, in the Vinnytsia region, the State Emergency Service of Ukraine said.Meanwhile, Ukraine hit a major missile fuel producer in Russia's Rostov region, which caused a fire and damaged four production facilities, Zelensky said.In Ukraine, repair works to restore power continued throughout the day. Most customers in the Dnipropetrovsk region had their connections restored by early evening, but more than 60,000 were still without power, the governor said.Because of regular attacks on energy infrastructure, emergency power cuts have been introduced across the country. Even in the capital Kyiv, electricity is cut off for most of the day, and water supplies are also disrupted.Zelensky said in a social media post that the intensity of Russian strikes has been "extremely high" over the past week, adding that Russia was "trying to take maximum advantage of the shortage of ballistic missile interceptors". He added that "every day" Ukraine communicated its need for Patriot missiles - the only effective weapon for downing Russia's deadly ballistic missiles - to the US, Europe and other partners. He thanked countries for their support so far and longer-term commitments, but called again for more immediate aid.

schema.headline: Russian strikes cut power to thousands in Ukraine as Kherson ceasefire ends
